calibration_text: This calibration passage describes a digital processor. Matrix tiles read numerical inputs and share stored keys between two query heads. A cache publishes a completed prefix only after its data and scale metadata are ready. Fixed parameters are learned before independent evaluation. Arithmetic uses explicit rounding and clipping, while a controller tracks token positions and immutable versions. This passage is calibration data, not a quality benchmark.

evaluation_texts.systems: A memory controller receives requests from several computing units. Each request names a sequence, a token position, and a previously published cache version. The controller must retain old keys while appending new values. It cannot change a stored scale without rewriting the affected data. We compare complete and incremental execution using identical tokens and record every numerical difference. No chip speed is inferred from this example.
evaluation_texts.arithmetic: Consider a small program that computes the sum of consecutive positive integers. The formula for the first n integers is n times n plus one divided by two. For n equal to seven the answer is twenty eight. A loop can produce the same answer by adding one number per step. Reordering dependent updates before the previous result is committed can produce an incorrect answer. This is an independent evaluation passage.

scale_contract: offline calibration-only shared g per KV group, static head K/V dyadic scale; Q per current row dyadic scale and M/r compiled offline; no evaluation refit
scope: local CPU Llama layer0 complete four-query GQA group plus bounded linear/RQ/port tests; no full model quality, all-integer model, RTL or physical speed
